Capacity (MW).note:
Capacity from the open Southwest Power Pool active queue file.

Where to find it:
- Open the file at https://opsportal.spp.org/Studies/GenerateActiveCSV and find the row with queue ID ERAS-2025-014. The row reads: Queue ID ERAS-2025-014, county column 'Hobbs', fuel column 'Combustion Turbine', facility type 'Thermal', owner column 'SPS', point of interconnection 'Hobbs-Andrews 345kV Line', status 'IA PENDING'. Its note column says 'Nameplate 234 MW, capacity 159.5 MW'.
- The 234 MW is the nameplate. The 159.5 MW is the capacity the grid operator credits, so we keep 234 MW.

Start year.note:
Start year from the same queue file.

Where to find it:
- Open https://opsportal.spp.org/Studies/GenerateActiveCSV and find queue ID ERAS-2025-014. The note column says 'Commercial operation date 2029-06-01'. The in-service date column shows 2028-05-31, which is the earlier date for grid connection.
- This is a projected year. The human adds a new scheduled event with Event Year 2029 and Source Year 2026, never by changing an existing one.

Turbine/Engine Technology.note:
The queue row calls the unit a combustion turbine.

Where to find it:
- Open https://opsportal.spp.org/Studies/GenerateActiveCSV and find queue ID ERAS-2025-014. The fuel column reads 'Combustion Turbine' and the facility type reads 'Thermal'.
- The queue does not give a make or model. I did not find one in the Southwestern Public Service 2026 resource plan or in the independent monitor's report.

units.notes: The open queue file confirms the 234 MW and 2029 values. I did not find the turbine make, a commission document naming this unit, a site address or a Backup Power statement. The status stays announced because no document I could read says construction started.

Owner(s).note:
The queue file names SPS as owner of this request.

Where to find it:
- Open https://opsportal.spp.org/Studies/GenerateActiveCSV and find queue ID ERAS-2025-014. The owner column reads 'SPS'. That matches GEM's current owner of Southwestern Public Service Co, so only the link is new.

qa.question: Can a person open the commission documents for the Hobbs gas turbine in case 25-00066-UT?
qa.finding: The commission approved Southwestern Public Service's gas additions on May 7, 2026, but no readable public document I found names the Hobbs turbine, its model or its site. A Utility Dive article from May 2026 at https://www.utilitydive.com/news/new-mexico-regulators-approve-sps-9b-gas-heavy-resource-plan/820978/ says 2,088 MW of gas was approved and does not name Hobbs.
qa.recommendation: Leave the unit as announced at 234 MW and 2029. Ask the project manager to open case 25-00066-UT in the commission's PRCe360 system and look for the turbine model and site.
qa.note:
What I read:
- The saved 2026 resource plan text for Southwestern Public Service (case 25-00076-UT) names the Hobbs Generating Station of 604 MW, a different plant, in its table of existing resources on its resource list, and the ERAS process on its page 51. It does not name a 234 MW unit.
- The independent monitor's final report on the 2025 request for proposals (case 23-00073-UT) discusses ERAS projects in general and gives no site.
- The New Mexico Environment Department permit harvest for this plant only lists the existing Hobbs Generating Station of Lea Power Partners, not a new turbine application.
- A lead site at https://www.infrasure.ai/project/spp-eras-2025-014 lists the entry at 160 MW, which matches the 159.5 MW credited capacity rather than the nameplate.
- Location was not worked because no document gives an address. The point stays approximate at 32.58532, -103.13716.
